_about.created: 26 September 2026; translated into English and edited for neutral wording on 11 October 2026
_about.method: Coded by one author from the full text, not by script. Each entry gives the location of the evidence in 'evidence'. 'not stated' means the text is silent, not that the step was not done. Entries are observations about what the papers report, for Table 1 of the accompanying manuscript; they are not judgements of the authors.

signs.a_collapse: a reported configuration shows signs of predicting one class: sensitivity ~100% with specificity ~0% (or the reverse), accuracy equal to prevalence, or identical rows across conditions
signs.b_leakage: the split unit is smaller than the patient: segments, overlapping windows, or channels of the same patient in both training and test sets
signs.c_inconsistent: reported numbers are arithmetically impossible for the test-set size, or contradict each other within the paper
signs.d_confound: a confounding factor coincides with the class: sampling rate 250 Hz (sddb) vs 128 Hz (nsrdb), pre-VF segment vs random minute, age

rows.study: Halim & Isa 2023, IJISAE (the first author's own article)
rows.test_n: 30 images according to the paper; 26 in the code folder (unexplained)
rows.all_models: yes: four models reported, including the collapsed ones
rows.a_collapse: YES: Tables 1 and 2 show Acc 53.94%, SN 100%, SP 0%, P 53.90%, F1 70.10% in almost every row, and two rows with the reverse (Acc 46.06%, SP 100%); the paper reads this as 'data we make is not suitable for LSTM'
rows.c_inconsistent: YES: mean precision 92.90% in the abstract vs 94.40% in Table 3; 18 normal records in the paper vs 17 in the code
rows.d_confound: YES: SCD three minutes immediately before VF, normal at random
rows.evidence: Tables 1-3 of the paper; code check in the repository scd-ecg-benchmark-audit
rows.note: First example of sign (a). Coded from the code check of 15 September 2026. Correction note: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23034462.

rows.interval: no: mean of 100 repeats without spread
rows.all_models: yes: 2 classifiers x 2 feature sets x with/without PCA, Tables 1-2
rows.b_leakage: YES: 'In cases that for each observation (patient), two channels were in access, each channel is used as a observation (patient)'; random split over channels
rows.d_confound: YES: SCD at 256 Hz, normal at 128 Hz (as stated in the paper); SCD minute immediately before death, normal minute at random
rows.note: sddb has 23 records, so 35 counts channels. The paper does not state whether PCA was fitted on training data only.

rows.study: Ebrahimzadeh et al. 2014, PLoS ONE (most cited study in the corpus; 139 citing works)
rows.unit: one minute per channel, four minutes before SCD
rows.validation: leave-one-out over 70 signals, repeated 16 times; feature selection inside the folds
rows.metrics: Acc, SN, SP, P; TP/TN/FP/FN per repeat
rows.interval: no: table of 16 repeats without a summary spread
rows.all_models: yes: Table 2 by feature set and classifier
rows.simple_baseline: no; the method of Shen 2007 is re-simulated for comparison
rows.b_leakage: YES: 'some patients with two channels ... both of them were used as input observations, so the total number of signals are 70'; leave-one-out over signals keeps the twin channel in the training set
rows.c_inconsistent: YES: Table 7 lists specificities of 0.001%, 0.037%, 0.089% and 0.159% beside accuracies of 99.73% to 83.93%; the values are consistent with false positive rates labelled as specificity (mean FP 0.062/70 = 0.0009)
rows.d_confound: YES: 256 Hz vs 128 Hz; normal subjects 5 men aged 26-45 and 13 women aged 20-50, SCD patients aged 18-89
rows.evidence: Materials and Methods paragraph 1; Classifier (LOO); Tables 3 and 7
rows.note: Feature selection is done inside leave-one-out, so channel duplication is the only leakage path.

rows.unit: beat ('Correctly classified SCD beats / Total SCD beats'); four minutes before SCD
rows.split_unit: not stated; beat is the unit
rows.b_leakage: possible: beats from the same patients, split not stated
rows.c_inconsistent: YES: Table 4 gives Sen 96.97%, Spe 99.2%, Acc 99.3%; accuracy is a weighted mean of sensitivity and specificity and cannot exceed both. Table 3 contains '89.34.2%'
rows.d_confound: partly addressed: all signals resampled to 128 Hz
rows.note: Table 4 cites Ebrahimzadeh et al. 2014 with Spe 98.27%, a value not printed in that paper. The paper states that the 20 records were used 'as they did not exhibit any episodes of VF', which is the reverse of the database description.

rows.split_unit: not stated; record is the unit, so leakage between segments is not possible
rows.all_models: yes: SVM and LR, all features / PSO / ANOVA
rows.b_leakage: not assessable: one excerpt per record; whether PSO feature selection was inside validation is not stated
rows.c_inconsistent: possible: accuracy 0.925 = 37/40 cannot be reached by a single test set drawn from 35 records; it may be a cross-validation mean, which is not stated
rows.d_confound: partly addressed: normal records upsampled to 250 Hz; SCD 5 minutes at 35 minutes before VF, normal at random
rows.note: Record counts conflict: 23 - 3 = 20, but the paper writes 20 and then excludes 3.

rows.study: Ebrahimzadeh et al. 2018, Trends in Research
rows.n_scd: 35 signals ('12 observations have been obtained from other channels')
rows.n_control: 35 ('17 observations have been obtained from other channels')
rows.b_leakage: YES: the second channel of the same patient is counted as a separate observation, as stated in the paper
rows.d_confound: YES: 256 vs 128 Hz; different age ranges
rows.evidence: Materials section; LOO paragraph; Tables 1 and 3
rows.note: The accuracies 99.73 / 96.52 / 90.37 / 83.96% are identical to those in Ebrahimzadeh et al. 2014 (PLoS ONE).

rows.unit: one-minute segment, 30 per record, 1,080 in total
rows.metrics: TP/TN/FP/FN, Sen, Spe, Acc, Prec, F1
rows.b_leakage: YES: 'we partition the instances to 5 parts'; an instance is a one-minute segment, 30 per record
rows.d_confound: YES: SCD 30 minutes before VF, normal from the middle of the recording
rows.note: Complete reporting makes the split unit clear from the paper itself. The data selection (records 40, 42 and 49 excluded for lacking VF; 38 and 41 for 'unknown lead') matches Lai et al. 2019.

rows.unit: one-minute segment, 30 per record, 1,380 in total
rows.metrics: Acc, Sen, Spe and others per classifier
rows.b_leakage: YES: 'a total of 1380 one-minute segments from 46 signals were divided into five parts equally'
rows.d_confound: YES: SCD 30 minutes before VF from two databases, normal from nsrdb; mean SCD age 60.65 years
rows.note: The same record exclusions appear in Reddy & Kumar 2022.

rows.study: Shi et al. 2020, Frontiers in Physiology
rows.unit: 2-minute HRV segment per channel, seven intervals
rows.validation: 10-fold CV, 'randomly divided into 10 mutually exclusive parts'
rows.all_models: yes: five ranking methods x 1-NN/10-NN, Tables 4-5
rows.b_leakage: YES: two channels per patient as separate signals (Table 1: 36 and 40 signals from 18 and 20 subjects), random split over signals; entropy parameters q and s chosen by t-test on all data
rows.d_confound: partly addressed: all signals resampled to 360 Hz
rows.evidence: data section and Table 1; 10-fold paragraph; Tables 2, 4, 5
rows.note: The arithmetic confirms that the unit is the channel signal: 97.5% requires a denominator of 40.

rows.unit: one-minute interval, 25 minutes before SCD; normal one minute at random
rows.validation: patient-level hold-out: 8 patients per class for training (45%), the rest for testing
rows.b_leakage: patient-level split; two indices selected by ANOVA p-values on all data before the split
rows.d_confound: YES: SCD 25 consecutive minutes, normal one random minute
rows.note: Table 3 contains only 90% and 100%, alternating, i.e. one or zero errors among about 10-20 test patients; the 94% is a mean of results that can take only two values. Training data were augmented with 400 uniform random values between the minimum and maximum of each interval.

rows.study: Tavazo & Ebrahimi 2025, International Journal of Engineering
rows.data: sddb + nsrdb + chfdb (15) as controls; cudb as external test
rows.unit: feature vector per one-minute interval, 60 minutes before SCD
rows.validation: 10-fold CV over 'the total number of feature vectors'
rows.split_unit: unclear: record level if one vector per record per interval, otherwise segment
rows.b_leakage: possible: MRMR selected 'locally for each one-minute interval', not stated to be inside the folds
rows.d_confound: partly: CHF controls reduce the patient-vs-healthy confound
rows.note: The only study in the corpus that adds diseased (CHF) controls. The external test on CUDB contains ongoing VT/VF episodes, which is a detection task rather than prediction.

rows.study: Shi et al. 2024, Research Square preprint
rows.b_leakage: YES: 'These ECG beats belonging to SCD subjects and normal individuals were divided into ten parts'
rows.note: Beat-level split with thousands of beats per patient. A journal version appeared in J Med Syst 2025 (doi:10.1007/s10916-025-02239-3), not read; its split may differ.

rows.study: Panjaitan et al. 2026, Journal of Information Systems and Informatics
rows.scd_stratum: S: three classes SCD, CHF, NSR
rows.validation: 80:20 subject-level hold-out; 'repeated 10 times' with a fixed random_state = 42
rows.metrics: Acc, Precision, Recall, F1, confusion matrix
rows.all_models: yes: SVM, DT, KNN, two scenarios
rows.b_leakage: no: 'All segments belonging to a single subject are assigned exclusively to either the training or testing set'
rows.d_confound: not checked: the position of the 15 minutes in the SCD records is not stated
rows.note: Subject-level split. 100% is reached on 11 test subjects; ten repeats with the same seed give the same split each time. The authors note that small, cleanly separated data 'can lead to inflated performance metrics, including repeated 100% accuracy'.

rows.study: Wu et al. 2026, Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine
rows.scd_stratum: S? (title says early prediction; the task is multi-class arrhythmia classification of 10-second segments)
rows.metrics: Acc, Prec, Rec, F1, Spe, FNR, FPR, AUC per class, confusion matrix
rows.b_leakage: YES, acknowledged by the authors: 'While segment-level separation was ensured, we acknowledge that strict patient-level separation remains a limitation'; 50% window overlap
rows.c_inconsistent: to check: recall 98.27% equals accuracy 98.27%, common for weighted means
rows.evidence: segmentation section (equation 3); validation paragraph; statistical test section
rows.note: A paired t-test on per-fold accuracy assumes independent folds, which cross-validation folds are not, especially with overlapping segments.

rows.scd_stratum: S: five classes NSR, CAD, CHF, VT, SCD
rows.data: sddb + nsrdb + chfdb + PhysioNet CAD and VT databases
rows.unit: 5-minute HRV segment, six per subject (30 minutes before VF for SCD)
rows.validation: 80/20 hold-out ('There were 115 subjects, with a training distribution of 80%')
rows.split_unit: unclear: the sentence names subjects, but the model input is the segment
rows.d_confound: YES: each class comes from a different database, with different sampling rates and recorders
rows.note: Models 3 and 4 report 100% training accuracy 'from the start' and 100% test accuracy from the first epoch, consistent with classes that are separable by a simple property such as database identity.

rows.study: Cha, Zhang, Zhang, Su & Lai 2024, Sheng Wu Yi Xue Gong Cheng Xue Za Zhi (Journal of Biomedical Engineering), 41(4), 692-699; PubMed 39218594
rows.data: sddb (20) + nsrdb (18); a source domain for pre-training
rows.validation: 10-fold CV: segments randomly divided into 10 subsets (Chinese text)
rows.b_leakage: YES: 30-second segments from 38 records randomly divided
rows.note: The values are identical to an IEEE PRML 2023 proceedings paper (doi:10.1109/prml59573.2023.10348344); the relation between the two versions was not checked.
